translation.title: Urea Cream
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for progressive keratoderma of the fingers (dry-type housewives' eczema), keratoderma of the palms and soles, ichthyosis, senile xerosis (dry skin in older adults), lichen pilaris, and atopic skin.
translation.usage: Wash the affected area, then apply this medicine 1 to several times a day and rub in thoroughly.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you have acute eczema or inflammatory skin disease, if you have renal failure, or on mucous membranes such as the membranes of the eye. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have inflammation or cracked skin, or if your skin has become highly sensitive to irritation. For external use only. Do not apply it directly to ulcers, erosions (raw skin) or wounds. Take care that it does not touch the eyes, nose, mouth or other mucous membranes; if it accidentally gets into the eyes, rinse thoroughly with plenty of water. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you use it together with corticoids, dithranol or 5-fluorouracil. Adverse reactions may occur - pain, a feeling of heat, sometimes flushing and itching; and hypersensitivity symptoms, sometimes eczematization, cracked skin, papules, a prickling feeling, a burning sensation and scaling, and rarely swelling and dryness; if any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Store at room temperature and keep out of reach of children.
